sources.entry: xmltodict - Makes working with XML feel like working with JSON.

summary.one_liner: xmltodict is a Python module that converts XML into Python dicts (and back) so XML can be handled like JSON.
summary.what_it_does: It parses XML strings, file-like objects, or generators of strings into nested Python dictionaries, with attributes stored under a configurable prefix (default '@') and text under '#text'. It can convert dictionaries back to XML with unparse(), optionally pretty-printed. Namespace handling is optional: process_namespaces=True expands namespace URIs and can collapse them to shorthand prefixes or skip them. A streaming mode uses an item_callback at a chosen depth so very large XML dumps can be processed with a small memory footprint. Options cover forcing lists or CDATA for selected elements, preserving comments, joining split text nodes, and post-processing parsed items.
use_cases: convert XML API responses into Python dicts
work with XML using JSON-style access
stream very large XML dumps item by item
generate XML from a Python dictionary
preserve XML attributes and text in dict form
cache parsed XML as dicts for reuse by scripts
notable: Streaming mode with item_callback at a given depth for huge files
Optional XML namespace expansion and prefix collapsing
force_list and force_cdata accept tuples or callables for fine control
Round-trip conversion between XML and dict via unparse()
Packaged by Fedora, Arch, Debian, FreeBSD, openSUSE, and conda-forge per README
caveats: Does not preserve every XML nuance such as attribute order, mixed content ordering, or multiple top-level comments; the README suggests lxml for exact fidelity
A CVE (CVE-2025-9375) was filed and is disputed by the maintainer, who considers it invalid; the README discusses element-name validation in XMLGenerator
